TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: How many players does a standard soccer team have on the field at once?
expl: A standard soccer team fields eleven players at once, including one goalkeeper. That's ten outfield players plus the keeper defending the goal. If a team drops below seven players, the match is typically abandoned. Soccer is the world's most popular sport, played in nearly every country. The modern rules of the game were first codified in England in 1863.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: In tennis, what is a score of zero called?
expl: In tennis, a score of zero is called "love." The term may come from the French "l'oeuf" (egg), which resembles the shape of a zero. Tennis scoring runs 15, 30, 40, then game, an unusual system dating back centuries. "Love" is used at every level, from beginners to Grand Slam finals. A "love set" means one player won all six games without losing a single one.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: In which country was modern badminton first codified?
expl: Modern badminton was first codified in England. It takes its name from Badminton House, the estate where the game grew popular. The sport actually has roots in ancient games from India and China. Badminton became an official Olympic sport in 1992. Its shuttlecock can travel over 400 km/h in professional smashes, faster than any other racquet sport.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
expl: The Olympic flag features five interlocking rings. They represent the five inhabited continents joined by the Olympic movement. The rings are colored blue, yellow, black, green, and red on a white background. At least one of these colors appears in every national flag in the world. The design was created in 1913 by Pierre de Coubertin, founder of the modern Olympics.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: In which sport would you perform a slam dunk?
expl: A slam dunk is performed in basketball. It became a signature move in the sport by the 1970s. College basketball briefly banned dunking from 1967 to 1976, partly due to Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's dominance. The Slam Dunk Contest, introduced in 1984, remains a highlight of NBA All-Star Weekend. Basketball itself was invented in 1891 by Dr. James Naismith using a soccer ball and peach baskets.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: What is the maximum possible score in ten pin bowling?
expl: The maximum possible score in ten-pin bowling is three hundred. A perfect game requires twelve strikes in a row. Bowling has been played in some form for thousands of years, with roots traced to ancient Egypt. Fewer than a thousand sanctioned "300 games" are recorded each year despite millions of games bowled. The triangular layout of ten pins has remained standard since the sport's modern rules were set in the 1890s.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which country has won the most FIFA World Cup titles?
expl: Brazil has won the most FIFA World Cup titles, with five championships. It's the only team to have played in every FIFA World Cup tournament. Brazil's most famous player, Pelé, remains the only person to win three World Cups. The country's yellow jersey is one of the most recognized kits in sports. Brazil hosted the tournament twice, in 1950 and 2014.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: In golf, what is the term for finishing a hole one stroke under par?
expl: A birdie is scored in golf, one stroke under par. Two strokes under par is called an 'eagle', and three under is an 'albatross'. The term "birdie" is believed to have originated in American slang for something excellent. Par itself represents the expected number of strokes a skilled golfer needs to complete a hole.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: How many periods are there in a standard ice hockey game?
expl: A standard ice hockey game is divided into three periods. Each period in professional ice hockey usually lasts 20 minutes. Teams switch ends between periods to balance any rink or lighting advantages. If the score is tied after three periods, the game may go to overtime or a shootout depending on the competition.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which sport is often nicknamed 'the king of sports' for being the most popular worldwide?
expl: Football, also known as soccer, is often nicknamed "the king of sports." It is the world's most popular sport, enjoyed by billions of fans and played in more than 200 countries and territories worldwide. The FIFA World Cup, held every four years, is the sport's most-watched single event. Football's simple rules and minimal equipment needs have helped it spread to nearly every corner of the globe.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: In the Olympics, which color medal is awarded for third place?
expl: A bronze medal is awarded for third place at the Olympics. Olympic medals must contain at least 92.5% silver, even the bronze ones are mostly copper alloy. Gold medals are actually made mostly of silver, coated with a thin layer of gold. The design of Olympic medals changes for each edition of the Games, reflecting the host city's culture.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: How many points is a touchdown worth in American football, before any extra point or conversion?
expl: A touchdown is worth six points in American football before any extra point or conversion. Teams can add one or two extra points after a touchdown through a kick or another play. A touchdown is scored by carrying or catching the ball in the opponent's end zone. The extra point kick is successful in the vast majority of cases at the professional level.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which combat sport involves trying to pin an opponent's shoulders to the mat?
expl: Wrestling involves trying to pin an opponent's shoulders to the mat. Wrestling is considered one of the oldest competitive sports, dating back thousands of years. It featured in the ancient Olympic Games as early as 708 BCE. Modern wrestling includes styles such as freestyle and Greco-Roman, each with different rules on holds and techniques.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: In football (soccer), what is it called when one player scores three goals in a single match?
expl: Scoring three goals in a single football (soccer) match is called a hat-trick. The term 'hat-trick' originally came from cricket, where a bowler took three wickets in a row. It was later adopted by football and other sports to describe any set of three achievements in one game. Fans sometimes throw hats onto the field to celebrate a player completing one.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: How many holes are typically played in one standard round of golf?
expl: A standard round of golf consists of 18 holes. A round of 18 holes became the standard at St Andrews in Scotland in 1764. Before that, golf courses varied widely in the number of holes they featured. Most 18-hole courses are divided into a "front nine" and a "back nine."

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: In swimming, which stroke involves face-down alternating overhead arm movements with a flutter kick?
expl: Freestyle is the swimming stroke that involves face-down alternating overhead arm movements with a flutter kick. Freestyle, also called front crawl, is generally the fastest swimming stroke. Swimmers are allowed to use any stroke they choose during freestyle events, though nearly all choose front crawl for speed. It is typically the first stroke taught to beginner swimmers.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which country hosted the very first modern Olympic Games in 1896?
expl: Greece hosted the very first modern Olympic Games in 1896. The first modern games were held in Athens, honoring the ancient Greek tradition. Only 14 nations and around 241 athletes competed in that inaugural Games. The event revived a tradition of athletic competition that dated back to ancient Olympia.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: In basketball, how many points is a single successful free throw worth?
expl: A single successful free throw in basketball is worth one point. A free throw is awarded after certain fouls and is taken unopposed from the foul line. Players typically get one, two, or three free throw attempts depending on the type of foul committed. The free throw line sits 15 feet from the backboard in most competitions.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which sport is traditionally played on a diamond-shaped field with four bases?
expl: Baseball is traditionally played on a diamond-shaped field with four bases. A baseball diamond actually forms a square, but is called a diamond due to its angle of view. The four bases are home plate, first base, second base, and third base. A batter must round all four bases to score a run.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: How many players are on a standard volleyball team on the court at one time?
expl: A standard volleyball team has six players on the court at one time. Volleyball teams also frequently rotate positions after winning a serve. The sport was invented in 1895 by William G. Morgan as a less strenuous alternative to basketball. A team must hit the ball over the net within three touches.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: In Formula 1 racing, what is the term for the starting position earned by setting the fastest qualifying lap?
expl: "Pole position" is the term for the starting spot earned by the fastest qualifying lap in Formula 1. Starting from pole position gives a significant advantage heading into the first corner. The term originated from horse racing, where the inside position near a track pole was considered the best start. Modern Formula 1 qualifying uses a three-part knockout format to determine the starting grid.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which Japanese martial art focuses mainly on throws and grappling rather than striking?
expl: Judo is the Japanese martial art that focuses mainly on throws and grappling rather than striking. Judo became an official Olympic sport for men in 1964. It was founded by Jigoro Kano in Japan in 1882. The word "judo" translates roughly to "the gentle way."

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: In cricket, what term describes a batter being dismissed when the ball hits the stumps directly?
expl: In cricket, "bowled" describes a batter being dismissed when the ball hits the stumps directly. A batter can be bowled even if the ball first grazes their bat before hitting the stumps. It is one of the most common ways to get a batter out in the sport. A "golden duck" occurs when a batter is bowled out on the very first ball they face.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: How many players make up a rugby union team on the field at one time?
expl: A rugby union team fields fifteen players on the field at one time. Rugby league, a related sport, instead uses only thirteen players per side. Rugby union developed at Rugby School in England, giving the sport its name. Matches are typically split into two 40-minute halves.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: Which winter sport involves sliding feet-first, lying face-up, down an icy track on a small sled?
expl: Luge is the winter sport involving sliding feet-first, lying face-up, down an icy track on a small sled. Luge athletes can reach speeds of over 140 kilometers per hour on the track. Unlike skeleton, where riders lie face-down, luge athletes lie on their backs. The sport has been part of the Winter Olympics since 1964.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: In which athletics event do competitors use a long pole to help clear a high horizontal bar?
expl: Pole vault is the athletics event in which competitors use a long pole to help clear a high horizontal bar. Modern pole vault poles are made of flexible fiberglass or carbon fiber, replacing the rigid wooden and metal poles used historically. The event has been part of the men's Olympic program since 1896 and the women's since 2000. Vaulters use the pole's bend to convert running speed into upward lift.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: What is the approximate distance, in kilometers, of a standard marathon race?
expl: A standard marathon race covers approximately 42 kilometers. The marathon distance is based on the legendary run from Marathon to Athens in ancient Greece. The exact modern distance, 42.195 kilometers, was standardized at the 1908 London Olympics. Marathons are now held in major cities worldwide, attracting both elite runners and amateurs.

TEXT_QUESTIONS.que: In snooker, which colored ball is worth the highest number of points?
expl: In snooker, the black ball is worth the highest number of points. A black ball in snooker is worth seven points, more than any other color. The colored balls are worth points ranging from one for red up to seven for black. Snooker is played on a large table with six pockets, using a cue and 21 balls plus the cue ball.

IMAGE_QUESTIONS.que: Which sport is played at Wimbeldon?

IMAGE_QUESTIONS.que: This tight-fitting eyewear and cap are worn by athletes in which sport?

IMAGE_QUESTIONS.que: This four-wheeled board, popular for street tricks, is used in which sport?

IMAGE_QUESTIONS.que: This wooden bat and leather glove are essential equipment in which sport?

IMAGE_QUESTIONS.que: These wooden stumps and bails are set up behind the batter in which sport?

IMAGE_QUESTIONS.que: This flaming torch is carried in a relay before the start of which global sporting event?

IMAGE_QUESTIONS.que: This long board, ridden while standing on ocean waves, is used in which sport?

AUDIO_QUESTIONS.que: Which sport uses this sharp whistle sound to start and stop play?

AUDIO_QUESTIONS.que: This dribbling and net-swish sound belongs to which sport?

AUDIO_QUESTIONS.que: This squeaky shoe sound is common on which type of playing surface?

AUDIO_QUESTIONS.que: This 'pock' sound of racket hitting ball belongs to which sport?

AUDIO_QUESTIONS.que: This ringing bell sound signals the start or end of a round in which sport?

AUDIO_QUESTIONS.que: This loud roaring crowd sound is typical of which large sporting event?

AUDIO_QUESTIONS.que: This sharp bang sound signals the start of which type of race?

AUDIO_QUESTIONS.que: This scraping-gliding sound on a frozen rink belongs to which sport?

AUDIO_QUESTIONS.que: This splashing sound is commonly heard at which type of sporting venue?

AUDIO_QUESTIONS.que: Which sports sideline activity features rhythmic chanting and clapping?

AUDIO_QUESTIONS.que: This rolling, rattling wheel sound on pavement belongs to which sport?
